findings.disposition: folded: terminal-panel capture scripts and the evidence fragment (scripts/prototypes/diiid_stopping_rule/, docs/evidence/fragments/diiid-vertical-force-balance/)
findings.summary: Frame 44's caption places the panel 'on the same limiter and levels' as frame 179, but the renderer derives each panel's seven contour levels from that frame's own flux grid (render_terminal_panels.py:130, linspace over that frame's finite min and span), and the two level sets share no value. Measured from the run's own artifacts: frame 179 limited flux spans -4.64467 to -0.18370 giving levels -4.199 to -0.630, while frame 44 limited spans -1.84483 to +1.68838 giving levels -1.492 to +1.335. Every contour on the frame-44 panel therefore sits at a flux value no contour on the frame-179 panel has, and since the panels carry no colourbar or level labels a reader has no way to see that. The sentence invites a like-for-like comparison of contour shapes that the figure does not support; it should say the panels share the limiter and the level rule, not the levels. The caption is not changed by this review.

The margin note under the legend is drawn in REFERENCE (#929292) at 13 pt, measured 3.11:1 against the note's white background, below the 4.5:1 that text of that size needs and below the 4.5:1 that the same figure's black legend text clears easily. It is the only text on the panels that states a wall-relative number, and on frame 137 it carries the set's only quantitative margin ('class margin -0.021'), so the least legible text holds the most load-bearing content. Fix is one colour argument at the note's construction, not a redraw.

Each panel is drawn on the declared 14 x 7.2 in, 100 dpi canvas (line 132) but bbox_inches='tight' then crops the saved raster to 735-766 x 635 px, and because the equal-aspect axes occupies only the left third of the figure the delivered image is 33-34% data and about 40% blank white to the right of and below the legend. At the page column width the poloidal cross-section renders roughly 260-300 px wide, which is small for a panel whose purpose is to be compared with its neighbours, and the four panels do not agree on canvas width (frame 137 is 31 px narrower because its note text is shorter), so they do not scale identically beside one another. A panel that fills more of its canvas, or a legend placed under the axes, would deliver the same information at a larger scale.

Three of the four panels print 'bounding surface: N vertices, class margin undefined' in the margin, so the only quantitative content in the image is empty on those three, while the captions carry the same measurement as a distance to the wall (0.043 m for frame 179, 0.061 m for 44, 0.048 m for 144). The renderer takes surface_class_margin from the geometry record and substitutes prose when it is not finite, which leaves the figure unable to distinguish a bounding ring that nearly touches the wall from one far inside it without reference to a caption. The value that does exist - the surface-to-limiter gap, which the script already computes for its report line - would make the three panels self-describing.

On frame 137 the EFIT X-point marker at R 1.27 m, Z -1.34 m is drawn in REFERENCE grey as a hollow cross inside a rotated square, and a 2.6 pt solved-flux contour runs horizontally through the middle of it while the grey dashed EFIT boundary passes just above, so at the delivered size the three grey-blue elements merge and the symbol is hard to identify without the legend. This is the marker the caption asks the reader to compare with the red solved X-point, in the one panel where the two null sets separate. It does not hide the separation (the red mark sits about 25 px below and is unmistakable), but the reference mark itself reads as a smudge at 1:1.

findings.disposition: exempted: the marks are plotted at their true coordinates and the size difference keeps the outer one visible; the caption states the coincidence, and separating them would falsify the geometry
findings.summary: Frame 144's solved X-point and EFIT X-point coincide at R 1.38 m, Z -1.06 m, so the red hollow cross is drawn over the grey one and the EFIT mark survives only as a grey halo around the red. The renderer anticipates this (render_terminal_panels.py:289-291 sizes the reference ring up so it reads around the solved marker) and the caption states that the two are drawn one over the other, so a reader who reads the caption is not misled and can see that both sets are present. Recorded because the panel alone does not let a reader count two marks, and any later re-render should keep the size difference.

justifications.durability: This record is written at both declared paths and checked with `reckon crew check --review --record` before the manifest is closed.
justifications.evidence: The level-sharing finding is measured from the run's own artifacts rather than inferred from the drawing code: the flux grids were loaded from probe-artifacts*/frame-44-limited-*.npz and frame-179-limited-*.npz and the script's own linspace formula applied, giving disjoint level sets. The contrast finding is a WCAG relative-luminance computation on the sampled note colour (#929292) against white. The clipping claim is the outer-frame pixel count, and the layout claim is a measured bounding box, not an impression.
justifications.legibility: Every verdict was read from the delivered raster at native size, with 2x-10x crops of the legend, the null markers and the margin notes taken from the same PNGs to resolve marks that are a few pixels across.
justifications.previously_recorded_findings: The earlier figure review of this run at head da9c18d8f recorded a blocking finding (no machine geometry drawn; the wall was the flux-grid bounding box), and further findings on dashed contours whose style carried no meaning, unidentified null markers, and only one null set plotted. At this head all four are answered on the picture: the real limiter polyline is drawn, all contours are solid, four null marks are named in the legend, and both null sets are plotted. The blocking finding is therefore resolved, which is why this review records no blocking finding.
justifications.scope_discipline: This review is read-only. No figure, caption, script or other repository file was edited, created, moved or reformatted; scratch crops were written only under the run's scratch directory. The only writes are this record at its two declared paths and the run manifest.
